import itertools

edges = list(itertools.combinations(range(7), 2))
edge_idx = {e: i for i, e in enumerate(edges)}

def solve():
    # 0 = red, 1 = blue
    # No red K_3 -> no 3 edges of color 0
    # No blue K_4 -> no 6 edges of color 1
    
    from pysat.solvers import Glucose3
    
    solver = Glucose3()
    
    # Variables 1 to 21
    # True = 1 (blue), False = 0 (red)
    
    # No red K_3
    for c in itertools.combinations(range(7), 3):
        e1 = edge_idx[(c[0], c[1])]
        e2 = edge_idx[(c[0], c[2])]
        e3 = edge_idx[(c[1], c[2])]
        # Not all 0 -> at least one is 1
        solver.add_clause([e1 + 1, e2 + 1, e3 + 1])
        
    # No blue K_4
    for c in itertools.combinations(range(7), 4):
        e1 = edge_idx[(c[0], c[1])]
        e2 = edge_idx[(c[0], c[2])]
        e3 = edge_idx[(c[0], c[3])]
        e4 = edge_idx[(c[1], c[2])]
        e5 = edge_idx[(c[1], c[3])]
        e6 = edge_idx[(c[2], c[3])]
        # Not all 1 -> at least one is 0
        solver.add_clause([-(e1 + 1), -(e2 + 1), -(e3 + 1), -(e4 + 1), -(e5 + 1), -(e6 + 1)])
        
    # Partial assignment
    # c[7]=1, c[8]=0, c[13]=0, c[14]=1
    solver.add_clause([7 + 1])
    solver.add_clause([-(8 + 1)])
    solver.add_clause([-(13 + 1)])
    solver.add_clause([14 + 1])
    
    if solver.solve():
        model = solver.get_model()
        return [1 if x > 0 else 0 for x in model]
    else:
        return None

print(solve())
